question: What specific divine command did the word of the LORD bring unto Jonah the son of Amittai concerning Nineveh in Jonah 1:1-2?
opt1: "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me"
opt2: "Go through the midst of Nineveh, and proclaim peace unto the king and his nobles, for their sorrow is noticed"
opt3: "Depart unto Nineveh with forty priests, and build an altar of unhewn stones to cleanse their abominations"
opt4: "Go forth to Nineveh, and seal the gates thereof with judgment, for their days are numbered by the LORD"
correct: "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me"
explanation: God commanded Jonah to cry against Nineveh due to its wickedness. Jonah 1:1-2 (KJV) - "Now the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying, Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me."

question: When Jonah rose up to flee from the presence of the LORD, to what destination did he seek passage, and at what seaport did he embark?
opt1: He fled unto Tyre, boarding a merchant galley at Ashdod after securing passage with silver
opt2: He fled unto Tarshish, boarding a ship at Joppa after paying the fare thereof
opt3: He fled unto Damascus, joining a caravan at Caesarea after purchasing camel provisions
opt4: He fled unto Alexandria, boarding an Egyptian grain ship at Gaza under an assumed name
correct: He fled unto Tarshish, boarding a ship at Joppa after paying the fare thereof
explanation: Jonah attempted to escape the divine presence by traveling west to Tarshish via Joppa. Jonah 1:3 (KJV) - "But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD."

question: While the terrified mariners cried each unto his god and lightened the tempest-tossed vessel by casting wares overboard, where was Jonah and what was he doing?
opt1: He was standing at the helm, praying silently to the God of Abraham to calm the wind
opt2: He was bound to the mast by the crew, weeping aloud in dread of the great waves
opt3: He had gone down into the sides of the ship, where he lay fast asleep
opt4: He was hiding beneath cargo in the prow, fasting and refusing to speak to the sailors
correct: He had gone down into the sides of the ship, where he lay fast asleep
explanation: In contrast to the frantic crew, Jonah slept deeply below deck. Jonah 1:5 (KJV) - "Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep."

question: With what urgent awakening rebuke did the shipmaster confront the sleeping prophet during the tempest?
opt1: "Why sleepest thou while the waves devour us? Awake, take up an oar and help us row to shore"
opt2: "Who art thou that slumberest in the hour of death? Cry unto the sea gods that they might spare our vessel"
opt3: "Dost thou not care that we perish? Arise and join our supplications unto heaven before the ship breaks"
opt4: "What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not"
correct: "What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not"
explanation: The shipmaster urged Jonah to call upon his God to prevent their perishing. Jonah 1:6 (KJV) - "So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not."

question: What method did the sailors employ to determine the individual responsible for the supernatural storm, and upon whom did the outcome fall?
opt1: They cast lots to know for whose cause the evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah
opt2: They questioned each passenger under oath before their idols, and Jonah confessed his guilt
opt3: They weighed the personal cargo of every merchant, and Jonah's chest proved cursed
opt4: They consulted an aboard astrologer who identified Jonah by the stars
correct: They cast lots to know for whose cause the evil was upon them, and the lot fell upon Jonah
explanation: God sovereignly directed the casting of lots to expose Jonah. Jonah 1:7 (KJV) - "And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah."

question: When interrogated by the mariners concerning his identity and heritage in Jonah 1:9, how did Jonah identify himself and his God?
opt1: "I am a prophet of Judah, and I serve the Almighty who ruleth over the kings of the earth"
opt2: "I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land"
opt3: "I am an Israelite of the tribe of Benjamin, and I worship the Lord God of hosts who dwelleth in Zion"
opt4: "I am a servant of the Most High, who commandeth the winds and whose throne is established in the heavens"
correct: "I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land"
explanation: Jonah confessed his Hebrew nationality and worship of Yahweh, Creator of sea and land. Jonah 1:9 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land."

question: When the sailors asked what they must do so the sea would be calm, what decisive remedy did Jonah instruct them to perform?
opt1: "Offer a burnt offering of clean sheep upon the upper deck, and the LORD will turn away his wrath"
opt2: "Turn the helm toward Nineveh and confess your sins, and the tempest shall instantly abate"
opt3: "Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you"
opt4: "Cast all remaining food and drink into the deep, and the anger of the God of heaven shall cease"
correct: "Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you"
explanation: Jonah recognized that only his being cast into the sea would appease the tempest. Jonah 1:12 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you."

question: Before throwing Jonah into the raging sea, what compassionate effort did the mariners make, and what prayer did they utter to the LORD?
opt1: They dropped heavy stone anchors and prayed that the sea would divide to let them pass safely
opt2: They offered silver coins into the waves and pleaded that Jonah's God would strike them blind instead
opt3: They tied life-lines to Jonah's waist and begged him to pray for mercy before casting him forth
opt4: They rowed hard to bring the ship to land but could not, and prayed that the LORD would not lay innocent blood upon them
correct: They rowed hard to bring the ship to land but could not, and prayed that the LORD would not lay innocent blood upon them
explanation: The sailors desperately tried to row ashore and pleaded with Yahweh not to hold them guilty of innocent blood. Jonah 1:13-14 (KJV) - "Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not: for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against them. Wherefore they cried unto the LORD, and said, We beseech thee, O LORD, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O LORD, hast done as it pleased thee."

question: What immediate dual effect followed the moment the sailors cast Jonah overboard into the raging waters?
opt1: The sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the LORD exceedingly, offering a sacrifice and making vows
opt2: A pillar of fire appeared above the water, and the sailors steered their vessel directly toward Jerusalem
opt3: The clouds parted revealing a brilliant rainbow, and the sailors fell prostrate and were baptized
opt4: The waves turned into crystal glass, and the shipmaster proclaimed a forty-day fast across all seaports
correct: The sea ceased from her raging, and the men feared the LORD exceedingly, offering a sacrifice and making vows
explanation: The sudden calming of the sea produced reverent fear and worship among the pagan mariners. Jonah 1:15-16 (KJV) - "So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging. Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the LORD, and made vows."

question: What creature did the LORD prepare to preserve Jonah, and for what exact duration was Jonah in its belly?
opt1: A mighty leviathan to transport Jonah, and Jonah remained in its belly forty days and forty nights
opt2: A great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights
opt3: A sea monster to protect Jonah, and Jonah dwelled in its inward parts seven days and seven nights
opt4: A royal whale to guide Jonah, and Jonah was in its depths twelve hours from twilight to dawn
correct: A great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights
explanation: God prepared a great fish where Jonah remained three days and three nights. Jonah 1:17 (KJV) - "Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights."

question: From where did Jonah pray unto the LORD his God, and how did he metaphorically describe the depths of his distress?
opt1: From the sandy seabed, declaring that he wept from the jaws of the dragon and the LORD answered him
opt2: From the dark underworld, proclaiming that he called from the pit of Abaddon and found peace
opt3: Out of the fish's belly, declaring that he cried out of the belly of hell and the LORD heard his voice
opt4: From the sunken abyss, testifying that he shouted from the chamber of silence and the angels responded
correct: Out of the fish's belly, declaring that he cried out of the belly of hell and the LORD heard his voice
explanation: Jonah prayed from within the fish, referring to his desperate plight as the belly of hell (sheol). Jonah 2:1-2 (KJV) - "Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly, And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice."

question: In Jonah 2:3, how does the prophet recognize God's sovereign hand in his immersion in the stormy ocean?
opt1: "Because the sailors flung me into the foaming tide, and the fierce winds tore away my strength and breath"
opt2: "For Satan sought to swallow up my soul in dark waters, and the dragons of the sea surrounded my limbs"
opt3: "Through mine own folly did I sink into the depths, and the unmeasured torrents carried me far from shore"
opt4: "For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me"
correct: "For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me"
explanation: Jonah recognized that it was God who cast him into the deep and that the billows were the LORD's waves. Jonah 2:3 (KJV) - "For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me."

question: What remarkable statement of faith did Jonah utter despite feeling banished from the divine presence in Jonah 2:4?
opt1: "I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple"
opt2: "I have perished from the land of the living; yet my bones shall declare thy righteousness"
opt3: "Mine eyes fail because of weeping; yet will I offer calves of praise upon thy mountain"
opt4: "Darkness hath covered my face; yet shall the light of thy countenance shine upon my grave"
correct: "I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple"
explanation: Even when cast out of sight, Jonah maintained faith that he would look toward God's holy temple. Jonah 2:4 (KJV) - "Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple."

question: What vivid physical description does Jonah provide in verse 5 regarding the constriction of the deep upon his person?
opt1: The fierce whirlpools sucked him downward, coral branches pierced his hands, and sand covered his nostrils
opt2: The waters compassed him about even to the soul, the depth closed him round about, and weeds were wrapped about his head
opt3: The ocean darkness blinded his sight, stinging sea jelly burned his flesh, and sea serpents encircled his waist
opt4: The crushing currents battered his body against sunken reefs, and great shells tore his garments into shreds
correct: The waters compassed him about even to the soul, the depth closed him round about, and weeds were wrapped about his head
explanation: Jonah describes the suffocating underwater descent where seaweeds tangled about his head. Jonah 2:5 (KJV) - "The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head."

question: To what subterranean depths did Jonah descend, and how did God intervene to save his life from corruption?
opt1: He sank to the foundations of the great abyss where iron gates locked him, yet an angel lifted him upon eagles' wings
opt2: He plunged into the subterranean roots of Lebanon where darkness reigned, yet God's voice shattered the granite doors
opt3: He went down to the bottoms of the mountains where earth's bars were about him forever, yet the LORD brought up his life from corruption
opt4: He reached the submerged caves of the dead where death held him fast, yet a bright light delivered him to the surface
correct: He went down to the bottoms of the mountains where earth's bars were about him forever, yet the LORD brought up his life from corruption
explanation: Jonah reached the extreme base of the mountains before the LORD miraculously brought up his life. Jonah 2:6 (KJV) - "I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O LORD my God."

question: What spiritual reflex sustained Jonah when his soul fainted within him, and where did his prayer ascend?
opt1: He recalled the covenant of circumcision, and his petition reached the cherubim above the mercy seat
opt2: He recited the psalms of David, and his supplication pierced through the celestial canopy of heaven
opt3: He remembered the promises given to Abraham, and his cry was recorded in the eternal book of life
opt4: He remembered the LORD, and his prayer came in unto God, into His holy temple
correct: He remembered the LORD, and his prayer came in unto God, into His holy temple
explanation: In his final extremities, Jonah remembered Yahweh and his prayer entered the heavenly temple. Jonah 2:7 (KJV) - "When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple."

question: What timeless theological principle regarding idolatry and grace does Jonah formulate in Jonah 2:8?
opt1: "They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy"
opt2: "Whosoever boweth down to carved images shall inherit eternal shame and sorrow"
opt3: "The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, having eyes that see not and ears that hear not"
opt4: "He that trusteth in vanity shall reap the whirlwind, and his hope shall perish like smoke"
correct: "They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy"
explanation: Those who pursue empty idols abandon the source of true covenant love and mercy. Jonah 2:8 (KJV) - "They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy."

question: With what resolve and attitude does Jonah commit to worship the LORD upon his anticipated deliverance?
opt1: "I will build an altar of fragrant cedar in Nineveh; I will proclaim thy name among all kings"
opt2: "I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed"
opt3: "I will offer ten thousand rams with singing; I will dedicate my firstborn son unto thy sanctuary"
opt4: "I will walk before thee in sackcloth and ashes; I will fast forty days in the wilderness of Judah"
correct: "I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed"
explanation: Jonah vows sacrifice with thanksgiving and the fulfillment of his solemn vows. Jonah 2:9 (KJV) - "But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD."

question: What climactic, foundational biblical doctrine concludes Jonah's prayer inside the fish's belly?
opt1: "The LORD reigneth for ever and ever"
opt2: "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts"
opt3: "Salvation is of the LORD"
opt4: "Great is thy faithfulness, O Lord God of Israel"
correct: "Salvation is of the LORD"
explanation: The ultimate soteriological truth uttered by Jonah is that salvation belongs wholly to Yahweh. Jonah 2:9 (KJV) - "But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD."

question: How did the great fish release Jonah after the LORD spoke unto it in Jonah 2:10?
opt1: It swam into the harbor of Joppa and opened its mouth for Jonah to walk out
opt2: It beached itself upon the rocks of Tarshish and expired as Jonah emerged
opt3: It carried Jonah up the Tigris River and deposited him at the gates of Nineveh
opt4: It vomited out Jonah upon the dry land
correct: It vomited out Jonah upon the dry land
explanation: At God's command, the fish vomited Jonah out onto dry land. Jonah 2:10 (KJV) - "And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land."

question: When the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, what specific charge was delivered to him?
opt1: "Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee"
opt2: "Go forth unto Nineveh, and write upon their city gates the impending judgments of the Almighty"
opt3: "Return to Joppa and testify unto the mariners, then journey northward to confront the Assyrian king"
opt4: "Arise, journey to Nineveh, and gather all the elders into the valley to announce forty days of silence"
correct: "Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee"
explanation: God reiterated His commission for Jonah to preach God's exact message to Nineveh. Jonah 3:1-2 (KJV) - "And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee."

question: How does the Scripture characterize the geographical scale and traversal size of Nineveh in Jonah 3:3?
opt1: It was a walled fortress requiring seven days of circumambulation
opt2: It was an exceeding great city of three days' journey
opt3: It was a sprawling metropolis covering twelve square leagues of fertile plain
opt4: It was an imperial capital containing a full month's journey of fortified suburbs
correct: It was an exceeding great city of three days' journey
explanation: Nineveh's massive scale is described as requiring three days to traverse. Jonah 3:3 (KJV) - "So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey."

question: After entering into Nineveh a day's journey, what brief yet ominous prophetic proclamation did Jonah cry aloud?
opt1: "Woe unto Nineveh, for fire and brimstone shall consume her palaces in three days"
opt2: "Repent, O Assyria, for the cup of the LORD's indignation runneth over upon thy streets"
opt3: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown"
opt4: "The sword of heaven is drawn; seventy days remain before thy complete destruction"
correct: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown"
explanation: Jonah proclaimed the impending overthrow of Nineveh within forty days. Jonah 3:4 (KJV) - "And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown."

question: How did the citizens of Nineveh respond to Jonah's warning in Jonah 3:5?
opt1: They arrested Jonah and delivered him to the temple of Dagon for trial under imperial law
opt2: They mocked the prophet openly and reinforced their city battlements with twenty thousand archers
opt3: They assembled their magicians and sorcerers to perform counter-divinations against the God of Israel
opt4: They believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them
correct: They believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them
explanation: The entire populace believed God and entered a state of national fasting and mourning. Jonah 3:5 (KJV) - "So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them."

question: What profound signs of personal humiliation and mourning did the King of Nineveh manifest when word reached him?
opt1: He arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes
opt2: He tore his royal crown into pieces, abdicated his throne, and fled into the mountains of Media
opt3: He commanded gold vessels to be offered to Yahweh, prostrated before the elders, and fasted forty days
opt4: He summoned the high priests of Ishtar, commanded their execution, and cloaked his palace in black silk
correct: He arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes
explanation: The monarch cast off imperial majesty to humble himself in sackcloth and ashes. Jonah 3:6 (KJV) - "For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes."

question: What comprehensive dietary decree was published throughout Nineveh by the king and his nobles in Jonah 3:7?
opt1: All wine and barley beer were forbidden for forty days, allowing only water and dry lentil bread
opt2: Neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, should taste any thing, feed, or drink water
opt3: Citizens were prohibited from eating meat or fruit, while livestock were driven into river pastures
opt4: Merchants were forbidden to sell leavened dough, and domestic beasts were fed only bitter herbs
correct: Neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, should taste any thing, feed, or drink water
explanation: The fast extended even to domestic animals, forbidding both food and water. Jonah 3:7 (KJV) - "And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:"

question: Beyond wearing sackcloth and crying mightily unto God, what crucial moral reform did the royal decree demand of every citizen?
opt1: To restore quadruple all stolen silver and free every Hebrew captive within the city walls
opt2: To dismantle every idol altar of Nisroch and erect a golden monument to the God of Jonah
opt3: To turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that was in their hands
opt4: To execute all corrupt judges and distribute royal palace granaries among the impoverished
correct: To turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that was in their hands
explanation: True repentance demanded turning from personal wickedness and systemic violence. Jonah 3:8 (KJV) - "But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands."

question: What poignant expression of hope in divine sovereign grace did the king articulate in Jonah 3:9?
opt1: "Surely the God of the Hebrews will accept our tears and reward our sacrifices with lasting peace"
opt2: "Peradventure the Almighty will show favor to the mighty empire of Assyria above all nations"
opt3: "Is not God obligated by our severe fasting to withhold the sword of vengeance from our homes?"
opt4: "Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?"
correct: "Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?"
explanation: The king recognized that God's mercy is an unmerited prerogative of His sovereign will. Jonah 3:9 (KJV) - "Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?"

question: What specifically did God observe in Nineveh that prompted His relenting from the proclaimed judgment?
opt1: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way
opt2: God saw the abundance of their sackcloth and the loud weeping of their children and cattle
opt3: God beheld the costly burnt offerings of bulls and sheep presented at the city gates
opt4: God saw the king prostrated upon the cold ground pleading forty consecutive days
correct: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way
explanation: God acknowledged their genuine repentance in works—turning away from evil. Jonah 3:10 (KJV) - "And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not."

question: What was the divine outcome recorded in Jonah 3:10 regarding the disaster threatened against Nineveh?
opt1: God postponed the judgment for three generations, granting them temporal respite
opt2: God repented of the evil that He had said He would do unto them, and He did it not
opt3: God sent an earthquake that damaged only their outer walls as a warning token
opt4: God commanded Jonah to sprinkle water upon the city gates to seal their pardon
correct: God repented of the evil that He had said He would do unto them, and He did it not
explanation: In response to their authentic turning, God relented and did not execute the destruction. Jonah 3:10 (KJV) - "And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not."

question: How did Jonah react when God showed mercy and spared the city of Nineveh?
opt1: Jonah rejoiced greatly and offered thanksgiving for the conversion of the Gentiles
opt2: Jonah fell upon his face and worshipped God for His wonderful lovingkindness
opt3: It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry
opt4: Jonah returned to Jerusalem in triumph to report the repentance of the Assyrian empire
correct: It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry
explanation: Jonah was deeply resentful that Nineveh was spared divine judgment. Jonah 4:1 (KJV) - "But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry."

question: What profound theological confession regarding God's character did Jonah cite as the very reason he originally fled to Tarshish?
opt1: "For I knew that thou art an holy God, consuming the wicked like stubble and showing no pity to uncircumcised nations"
opt2: "For I feared the cruelty of the Assyrians, lest they flay my skin and hang my head upon the walls of Nineveh"
opt3: "For I perceived that thy word would fail, and my reputation as an accredited prophet of Israel would be ruined"
opt4: "For I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil"
correct: "For I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil"
explanation: Jonah admitted he fled because he knew God's boundless grace would spare the penitent. Jonah 4:2 (KJV) - "And he prayed unto the LORD, and said, I pray thee, O LORD, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil."

question: In his bitter despondency in Jonah 4:3, what drastic petition did Jonah make unto the LORD?
opt1: "Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live"
opt2: "Cast me once again into the tempestuous sea, for I cannot bear to behold Nineveh flourishing"
opt3: "Blind mine eyes, O LORD, that I may never look upon the children of Assyria dwelling in peace"
opt4: "Send down fire from heaven upon mine own head, for my ministry hath brought shame upon Israel"
correct: "Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live"
explanation: Despairing over God's mercy toward enemies of Israel, Jonah asked to die. Jonah 4:3 (KJV) - "Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live."

question: With what gentle, penetrating question did the LORD initially challenge Jonah's petulant anger in Jonah 4:4?
opt1: "Why weepest thou over a city that hath repented?"
opt2: "Doest thou well to be angry?"
opt3: "Is mine arm shortened that I may not show mercy?"
opt4: "Hast thou forgotten the belly of the great fish?"
correct: "Doest thou well to be angry?"
explanation: God gently rebuked Jonah by questioning the righteousness of his anger. Jonah 4:4 (KJV) - "Then said the LORD, Doest thou well to be angry?"

question: Where did Jonah position himself after leaving the city, and what shelter did he construct while waiting to see Nineveh's fate?
opt1: He camped on the western ridge beneath a tent of goat hair, watching for lightning to strike Nineveh's citadel
opt2: He ascended the northern hills and built a stone watchtower, praying for fire from heaven to fall
opt3: He sat on the east side of the city under a booth he made, waiting in the shadow to see what would become of the city
opt4: He lodged in a cave overlooking the Tigris River, fasting until the forty days were fully accomplished
correct: He sat on the east side of the city under a booth he made, waiting in the shadow to see what would become of the city
explanation: Jonah went to the east of Nineveh and built a booth to watch the city. Jonah 4:5 (KJV) - "So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city."

question: What plant did the LORD God prepare to provide shade over Jonah's head and deliver him from grief, and what was Jonah's reaction?
opt1: A wild fig tree that yielded sweet fruit, and Jonah praised God with songs of thanksgiving
opt2: A broad-leafed cedar that shielded him from wind, and Jonah resolved to remain there forty days
opt3: A leafy grapevine that provided abundant shade, and Jonah fell peacefully asleep under its branches
opt4: A gourd (plant) to shade his head and deliver him from grief, and Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd
